title: End Of Abyss Patch Fixes Most Of My Complaints Just One Day After Launch
text: I spent a few days playing Section 9 Interactive's creepy metroidvania and writing my End of Abyss review , and ultimately concluded it was a fun but inconsistent experience hindered by a few particular issues. Now, just a day after it launched on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via the Epic Games Store, the studio has already cleared up most of those issues with a newly released patch . If you missed the review, my main concern was how the in-game map would sometimes share incorrect information, like telling me a door was locked when I had unlocked it, or failing to signify when I'd found the key to a particular door. In a metroidvania, this means a whole lot. End of Abyss is a game about exploration, including lots of backtracking via roundabout paths, so when I'd plan long treks across the world based on a faulty map, it was really frustrating to find out too late that I'd essentially been lied to. But a patch has fixed that, among other problems, and it presents an uncommon issue for me. My review only went out two days ago. The game only launched yesterday. Now much of my review is already outdated. In this era of live-service games and post-launch updates, it's common for games to change shape over time, but for End of Abyss's patch to fix many of its lesser parts essentially right after the deadline isn't normally how it goes. Usually big, important changes happen in one of two ways: In one common scenario, a game that critics are playing for review may be patched during that pre-release review period. It's often the case that critics are made aware of bugs we might see, and we're usually told when they've been patched out, or that those fixes are in the "day one" patch that comes with the game's public launch, leaving us to confirm as much once the patch drops. This even applies to End of Abyss. I bumped into a few bugs during my time with the game, and the very worst of them--in which a boss failed to drop a quest item--was patched just a few hours before I had to write my review, allowing me to beat the game on time. This made the issue irrelevant to my review, and thus I didn't even specifically call it out. If the public wasn't going to experience it, then I take it as my job to basically erase it from my memory of the experience--or at least, if I do mention it, I should explain how it's no longer a concern for players jumping in at launch. In another common scenario, a game changes shape much later in its lifespan, and probably over the course of several updates. Games like Sea of Thieves, Overwatch, and Fallout 76 are great examples. These kinds of games often become the subject of re-reviews years later. But it's not just multiplayer games that do this. Games such as Starfield, Mass Effect 3, and Cyberpunk 2077 have been affected by such major changes that they merited follow-ups, too. But End of Abyss is a much rarer case. The game just came out. My review could only speak to my experience, and so it does, but I'd planned to revisit it once my biggest problems with it were addressed and write something like what I've written here--something that says, "Hey, it's better now!" when I could recommend it with more confidence. I just didn't expect that would be a mere 48 hours after I published my thoughts on the game. Section 9's debut landed in a weird gray area, where some important fixes came neither early enough for my review to consider them, nor late enough for my review to feel like it accurately reflected the experience of playing the game for a reasonable period of time. As it stands, only the players who jumped in yesterday--likely a relative few compared to the many more who will play the game over the next several years--bumped into the map issue I had during my time with it. No one else will ever have to deal with it. That's good for players, and good for the studio, even if it leaves reviews like mine feeling more swiftly outdated than anything I can remember writing.

title: GTA 6 Screenshot Suggests It Won’t Be Shy About Movie References
text: A new screenshot from Grand Theft Auto 6 has arrived, and fans immediately noticed that it appears to be referencing the iconic opening scene from Quentin Tarantino's 1994 crime movie Pulp Fiction. The image was shared by Love magazine on Instagram . The GTA 6 Countdown social media account put it next to the diner scene from Pulp Fiction, and the similarities are there, especially in the framing. In Pulp Fiction, Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer's characters, Pumpkin and Honey Bunny, go on to rob the diner, and given that Lucia and Jason are criminals as well, it's not a stretch to think that could happen in GTA 6. Maybe they're just enjoying breakfast, but that seems unlikely given the image clearly shows both gripping their pistols, with Lucia seemingly ready to fill the empty duffel bag next to her with cash and other valuables. https://twitter.com/GTAVI_Countdown/status/2106042257443049741 GTA 6 tells a Bonnie and Clyde-style story of two lovers who are also criminals. Things did not end well for them, and many are speculating as to how GTA 6's story could wrap up for both Lucia and Jason. It also wouldn't be surprising to see GTA 6 reference Pulp Fiction given how GTA games in the past have featured very overt references to movies, like how Vice City had Scarface references and GTA 5 had nods to Heat. "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,”GTA 6 writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love magazine. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.” Jason and Lucia in GTA 6. Another GTA 6 game writer, Alexa D’Agostino, told the magazine, “When you are focusing on writing a fully realized person with their own wants, you’re going to get something perfectly imperfect--with clichés, but also undeniably real.” GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. On November 18, the Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys and play on a court that references Vice City, the game's setting, and a stand-in for Miami. GTA 6 will take players outside of Miami to other places in Florida, just don't expect to go to Rockstar's version of Walt Disney World .

title: The Xbox Cloud Gaming Controller Is Not Dead, Apparently
text: Microsoft agreed to several big changes to appease regulators in its effort to get the blockbuster $75.4 billion deal to buy Activision Blizzard approved, including tweaks to its cloud-gaming projects. Now, more than a year later, we're still learning more about this, including a new claim from The New York Times that Microsoft canceled plans for a new Xbox controller "devoted to cloud gaming." A spokesperson for Microsoft denied that the controller concept was abandoned due to the regulatory process. Separately, sources told Windows Central that "rumors that Microsoft has canceled upcoming Xbox Cloud Gaming controllers are false." Microsoft never formally announced or unveiled any controller for cloud gaming, but an image of it leaked this year, prompting raised eyebrows for its ... unique design. Microsoft cut deals with a variety of companies--including Ubisoft , Nware , EE, Boosteroid , Ubitus , and Nvidia --to help mitigate concerns from the UK's Competition & Markets Authority (CMA) that Microsoft might give preferential treatment to its own cloud gaming networks. Former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer, who led Xbox during the sale process, said such deals freed up one of the concerns the CMA had and helped bring more games to more people. The Xbox cloud-gaming service showed some initial signs of growth , but the program suffered a setback recently when Microsoft announced that it will soon put limits on how much people can use the service , and then charge them more to keep playing. Additionally, Windows Central recently discovered that the dedicated cloud gaming app for older Samsung TVs will go away soon due to a compatibility issue. The site later reported that the support for older Samsung TVs is due to "the lack of updates those sets are getting" as Samsung focuses on its newer units. Additionally, sources told Windows Central "there are absolutely no plans to decelerate on Xbox Cloud Gaming" generally. Access to cloud gaming is one of the perks of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, allowing people to stream their games. Later this year, people will be able to buy game time for cloud gaming on Xbox without a Game Pass membership. One of the appeals of cloud gaming, at least in theory, is that it requires no expensive local hardware like an Xbox or PC, both of which are more expensive than ever due to the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. People need a consistent and fast internet connection for the best experience. In other Xbox news, CEO Asha Sharma recently stressed that Xbox is "not for sale," following rumors and reports that Microsoft could unload the struggling company.

title: GTA 6 Should “Blaze A Trail” To More Expensive Games, Dev Says
text: Rockstar's GTA 6 is priced at $80 for its standard edition. Another voice has come forward to say they hope other teams follow suit and charge more for new games to help the industry at a time when developers are closing up shop, cancelling games, and laying off developers on a regular basis. Martin Klima, the co-founder of Kingdom Come developer Warhorse, told PC Gamer that raising unit prices would "help a lot," but "everybody's scared to death" to do it. "Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost," he said, adding that Rockstar and Take-Two are among the only companies who can "afford, or who can dare" to raise prices in this way. He added that price increases for new games are "long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive." GTA 6 should kick off a trend of games costing more, Warhorse co-founder says. Take-Two was among the first big publishers to drive prices up from $60 to $70, kicking this off with NBA 2K21 in 2020. Numerous other publishers followed suit, and now $70 is the norm. Defending the price increase, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said production costs increased by 300%. Former PlayStation executive Shawn Layden said in 2025 that the price of new games should have gone up with every new console generation for the past 20 years. That largely did not happen, and now the industry is worse off for it, he said. “I think it’s because everyone’s afraid,” he told GI.biz . “No one wants to be the first one to raise the price, because you’re afraid to lose traffic. So what you do is you just end up eating into your operating income, your profit margin.” “There were more sports cars in the parking lot in the PS1 era than there were in the PS4 era, because if you’re selling 20 million units at $60 for something that only cost you $10 million to make, that’s different than selling 20 million units at $60 for something that cost you $160 million to make.” To help make up the difference, developers have hawked things like microtransactions, DLC, and battle passes . If more games go up in price, those trends will likely continue, too. Before GTA 6's price was revealed, a Bank of America stock analyst said Take-Two should charge $80 to help spur other publishers to follow suit . We already have $80 games, as Nintendo charges $80 for Mario Kart World, saying the game's ambition justifies the price tag . Every game is priced differently, even within the same publisher, as Take-Two launched Mafia: The Old Country for $50– to great success . For its part, Nintendo's newly released F ire Emblem: Fortune's Weave costs $80 for its physical edition or $70 for its digital counterpart. GTA 6, which releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, also has a $100 Ultimate Edition and a $400 collector's edition that does not include the game. Zelnick said earlier this year that Rockstar could have leveraged the monumental demand for GTA 6 to c harge a higher price to consumers , but chose not to. In addition to the mountains of money Rockstar and Take-Two are due to make off GTA 6 game sales, the game is likely to eventually have some kind of new version of GTA Online, and that's no doubt going to print money .

title: GTA 6 Takes The Ridiculous World We Live In And Turns It Up To 11
text: Video games are usually a few steps removed from reality, but with Grand Theft Auto 6 , developer Rockstar Games aims to reflect and amplify the current state of the world with an "over the top" experience. As seen in the trailers and gameplay previews so far, GTA 6 is a contemporary game about doing whatever it takes to make it to the top, and that pursuit of fame and glory is often bookended by shootouts, car chases, and explosions in its Bonnie and Clyde narrative. "If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face," senior VP of narrative Rupert Humphries said to Love Magazine . "Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world." Humphries also described the world of GTA 6 as "a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity," as the protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, are polar opposites. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern described Lucina as an ambitious go-getter who'll do anything to get the life she dreams of, while Jason is bound by life's circumstances. "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other," Gauvey-Kern said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_vlzIPpyJR0 GTA 6 is also making some big changes to the franchise formula, as getting out of trouble won't be as easy as hiding in an alley and waiting for your wanted level to drop. Actions have consequences, and with the cops being much smarter and more persistent, players will have to be more cunning before they embark on a crime spree. The relationship between Jason and Lucia is also surprisingly more nuanced and deeper than you think, and it'll be a major part of the overall GTA 6 experience when the game launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. With the wait almost over, the marketing machine for GTA 6 has begun to get into gear. Advertising has already taken over a Miami stadium , and the NBA's Miami Heat have announced they'll wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they face off against the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18. Rockstar Games also announced a $400 GTA 6 Collector's Edition last week; while it doesn't include the game, it does include various trinkets typically associated with users of the devil's dandruff. title: In 5 Years, Will Netflix Still Be In Gaming? Here’s What The CEO Said
text: Netflix has been experimenting with video games for a while, but is the streaming giant going to eventually drop out of gaming? That's the question Bloomberg's Lucas Shaw put to Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos at the Screentime event this week . Regarding whether Netflix will still host games in five years, Sarandos said, "I think so." He said Netflix's push into mobile gaming was "a gateway to cloud gaming," which is something Netflix is "much more interested in." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1lsV9I2NDO8 Netflix hosts a variety of mobile games, including Red Dead Redemption, Sonic Mania Plus, and RollerCoaster Tycoon Touch, just to name a few. The games are included with a Netflix membership and have no ads. Netflix also hosts streaming games that can be played on your TV, and they are more family- and party-focused. Netflix's gaming ambitions have bounced around over the years. At one point, the company wanted to make big, AAA games, and hired some big names to get it done. However, Netflix later wound down these efforts , closing studios and laying off staff in the process, leading many to wonder what Netflix's ambition for video games actually was. Sarandos said cloud gaming makes more sense for Netflix "in a post-console world." He didn't elaborate here, but it sounds like he's talking about a future where more and more people play games without dedicated hardware like a PlayStation, Xbox, or Switch console. All of those systems have gone up in price in recent times due to AI-fueled component and memory issues, along with bigger global macroeconomic trends. The cloud gaming market hasn't popped the way some have predicted, but Sarandos isn't the only person who is optimistic about the future potential. Strauss Zelnick, the head of GTA 6 owner Take-Two recently said , "I think we'll be in commercial streaming mode within three years." Sarandos said there will be "all kinds of opportunities for gaming on the television," and the executive said Netflix wanted to be "early invested in that." "I like it for IP extension. I certainly like it for brand value, for people who want to spend time on that screen gaming instead of watching, then we have an option for them," he said. Also in the interview, Sarandos was asked if Netflix would again reach into its coffers to buy a large-scale gaming company to help its gaming ambitions become realized faster. The interviewer asked if Netflix could buy Take-Two or Xbox, and Sarandos said it doesn't have any specific plans to buy more gaming studios, though he's not ruling anything out either. For what it's worth, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma recently said Xbox is not for sale , while Take-Two selling itself would be shocking. Sarandos said Netflix prefers to grow organically instead of buying companies to spur growth. Of course, this isn't a hard-and-fast rule, as evidenced by Netflix offering to buy Warner Bros. Discover for many billions of dollars before Paramount swooped in and made a deal. He said Netflix went after WBD because the company was "so clean" and contained only the elements and assets of the business that Netflix actually wanted, and that was rare. Netflix will look at other opportunities to buy game studios if they complement the company's wider business goals, Sarandos said. In other news about cloud gaming, Microsoft has reportedly canceled its new controller for it , ahead of price hikes to the service soon . Netflix has also said it's still very early days for its gaming output, saying the company has “tons more work to do." Netflix's financial investment in gaming is minuscule relative to its other business areas, and management sees gaming as a "significant market opportunity." Netflix investors no doubt want to see Netflix find new ways to make money; after all, Netflix stock has crashed more than 25% in 2026 so far.

title: Sony’s Revised PS5 Slim Could Be Getting Cheaper To Make, But Not To Buy
text: It looks like Sony has quietly revised the PS5 console once again, with new internal changes across the (mother)board. It's not clear when these new models came into service, but they seem to have entered circulation around the same time Sony released limited-edition Marvel's Wolverine PS5 consoles. Spotted by Modyfikator89, longevity and repairability appear to be the key areas that Sony has focused on. The redesigned motherboard offers easier access to the CR2023 battery, the streamlined internal layout makes repairs less risky, and the hardware takes a page from the PS5 Pro playbook with refined liquid-metal containment and revised heatsink materials. In theory, the updated barrier around the processor die should keep the liquid metal better contained over time, ensuring stable thermal transfer performance even under intensive loads. https://twitter.com/Modyfikator89/status/2105382987755814984 Sony has also moved to a newer, lower-cost HDMI retimer chip, which likely cuts down bill-of-materials costs and improves display signal stability. Overall, this will likely lower production costs while maintaining higher assembly yields, at a time when sourcing components has become more challenging. Companies routinely make stealth revisions to cut manufacturing costs, but unlike previous console generations that shrank and became cheaper over time, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive since it launched in November 2020. When it first launched , the entry-level PS5 Digital Edition had an MSRP of $400, but in 2026, you can expect to pay $600 for one. The base model PS5 with a disc drive has increased from $500 to $650, while the PS5 Pro has shot up from $700 to $900. Sony is aiming to make the PS5 a better value proposition as it heads into the lucrative holiday season, after recently launching a new AI-upscaling technology for its base-model PS5s. Only two of its exclusive games support it currently--Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei--and the technology will be released to more developers soon. By enabling the base PS5 to deliver sharper visuals through Quick Spectral Super Resolution, Sony offers a visual upgrade in select games without having to splash out on the more expensive PS5 Pro.

title: NBA’s Miami Heat Will Wear GTA 6 Jerseys And Play On A Branded Court The Day Before Release
text: The NBA's Miami Heat have announced that they will wear GTA 6 -inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, a day before the game releases. Additionally, the game will take place on a "never-before-seen court," and it'll be inspired by GTA 6 and Vice City. The Heat play at the Kaseya Center in Miami, which was recently adorned with "Vice City" signage, airlifted in by helicopter . The game will air on ESPN on November 18. Tickets are on sale now . https://twitter.com/MiamiHEAT/status/2106007519545974792 There will also be "special activities" and "unique game night activations" on November 18 that the team will detail later. The new Heat jerseys and court design will also be revealed later. As for what's available now, the Heat have rolled out a "Vice City Collection" of merch, including a $55 t-shirt that says, "Went to Vice City and all I got was this lousy t-shirt" and a $45 shirt that says, "I love Vice City." You can see the full collection at the Heat's online store . The November 18 matchup is also notable because Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo is playing against his former team, the Bucks, where he had spent his entire career until this season. Rockstar is spending big money to advertise GTA 6 in Miami, and some local officials have expressed concerns . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game has reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies, generating more than $570 million in pre-sales. Also this week, Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 will have more than 170 animal species , including cane toads and monkeys. We also learned that GTA 6 has a new dynamic weather system .

title: Blizzard Might Finally Be Serious About WoW: Forever Gold Buying, Bans Streamer For Promoting It
text: A prominent World of Warcraft: Forever streamer has been banned following comments made on stream encouraging his viewers to buy gold on his behalf. Forever, which is currently in beta ahead of the MMORPG's full launch in November, is currently mired in a gold buying and real-money transaction (RMT) controversy. Players buying gold from third-party websites that use bots to farm the game's primary currency has been a problem for the entirety of WoW's existence and has always been against the game's terms of service. What's changed is that developer Blizzard has made comments that it's looking to more aggressively punish gold buyers in Forever, even going as far to admit its been too "lenient" on the matter in the past. That more hardline stance against gold buyers was put to the test earlier this week when WoW: Forever streamer Ziqo was seen on stream accepting suspiciously large amounts of gold from strangers in the lead-up to a $100,000 prize pool PvP tournament he and many other streamers will be competing in. Given the huge sums of gold being traded, many believed there was little chance the gold had been acquired naturally through farming and was likely bought by a third party and then given to Ziqo as a gift. https://youtu.be/dvueCoFTkCk?si=YqPAFYzvWt5J5WiC Almost immediately, the Forever community was up in arms demanding Blizzard take action. In a forum post seemingly issued in response to the Ziqo controversy, Blizzard stated that it would increasingly punish not only gold sellers, its standard practice, but also those buying the gold. In addition, accounts accepting large amounts of questionable gold could also be punished by having the illicit gold removed, their account suspended, or even permanently banned. Blizzard encouraged players not to accept "suspicious" transactions to avoid these consequences. Even if Ziqo wasn't the buyer, according to Blizzard's own words, he could in theory be punished for taking what many viewed to be ill-gained gold. That same gold in question was later removed from Ziqo's account by Blizzard, though the streamer was not banned or suspended, as many players called for. https://www.reddit.com/r/classicwow/comments/1wtnmfr/i_never_hid_the_fact_that_i_wanted_my_chat_to_buy/?share_id=zh96vvQnxd9xojUBRfqN7&utm_content=share_button&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_source=share&utm_term=1 The same can't be said for another WoW streamer looking to participate in the game's upcoming tournament, Payo. Amidst the Ziqo drama, Payo said on stream he hadn't been shy about the fact he is more than okay with members of his community buying gold on his behalf. "I never hid the fact I want my chat to use their credit cards to fill my bags," Payo said on stream. Those comments look to have caught Blizzard's ire, as it was only a few days later that Payo's account had been banned from the game. He has since apologized and said he's never bought gold personally. He said he was "happy" about the ban, because it shows Blizzard is serious about the RMT problem. Though his main account was banned, Payo was not banned permanently and was allowed to create another account and continue streaming Forever. "I learned from my mistake, and I will never ever promote gold buying again, that's for sure," Payo said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XKtc_UCcmZA In the wake of Payo's ban, Blizzard issued another warning shot of a forum post . Community manager Kaivax in a post on October 1 said Blizzard has continued to take action against botting accounts and those who have bought or "knowingly received illicit gold." In addition, Kaivax announced Blizzard will be adding a warning to Forever that will appear when trading with strangers. The warning that will appear is as follows: "Be wary of accepting gold from unknown or suspicious sources. If the provider is engaged in Real Money Transactions, you could put your account at risk of closure." Kaivax concludes by making Blizzard's stance on RMT "crystal clear:" "Any account belonging to any player that is found to have participated in generating, selling, buying, or receiving illicit gold is subject to the gold being removed, account suspensions, or permanent account closers." Some players on places like the WoW Classic subreddit are still skeptical. Blizzard has always talked a big game about banning bots, for example, but as any WoW Classic player can tell you, botting is still a major issue. More than a few in the community point to the fact that Payo and Ziqo weren't permanently banned as Blizzard still being too lenient, especially towards streamers. For others, Blizzard going as far as adding an actual in-game warning about the dangerous consequences of engaging with RMT is a major escalation in the war against gold buyers and sellers. "Players are being given plenty of warning," user Dessiato said in a post discussing Kaivax's forum post. "I look forward to the reckoning." Whether Blizzard lives up to its word remains to be seen, but there's no doubt the Forever beta is putting WoW in the spotlight in a way that hasn't been seen since the launch of WoW Classic in 2019. Blizzard developers have commented that the Forever beta is breaking records , with the Forever beta population cap needing to be raised multiple times since its launch on September 17. The beta, which requires the purchase of the $60 Skyborne Heroic pack in order to gain access , will run until October 21. WoW: Forever launches in full November 4.

title: Disney Responds To Rumor That It Could Buy Fortnite Studio Epic Games
text: One juicy gaming rumor that continues to swirl is that The Walt Disney Company could buy Epic Games and Fortnite. It remains to be seen if such a deal may materialize, and now a top boss at the House of Mouse has directly responded. Speaking at Bloomberg's Screentime event this week, Disney executive Dana Walden reminded everyone that Disney already i nvested more than $1.5 billion into Epic for an equity stake . But could talks progress to a full acquisition? "Those are not the conversations we're having right now," Walden said. "But we have a great partnership." Disney and Epic are working together to create “transformational” new games . So far, they have showed up in Fortnite in a variety of ways, including the recent integration of Fortnite at Disney's real-world parks . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yf2bRcSIUsE Walden said people can look forward to even more to come in the next few years. "A number of launches coming up over the next two years ... are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership," she said. Kevin Mayer–a former Disney and TikTok executive who now runs Candle Media–said Disney's new CEO, Josh D’Amaro, will need to take “bold steps” to help Disney make more money and grow its stock price. One part of this could be buying Epic Games or another game studio , he said. Technology reporter Alex Heath recently said on Matthew Belloni’s podcast, The Town , that he knows “for a fact” that some senior executives at Disney want to buy Epic Games and are waiting for the right moment. Other executives at Disney believe it would be a bad idea, Heath said. Epic Games is a founder-controlled company, with CEO Tim Sweeney retaining full voting stock control. He has the ability to make unilateral decisions to control and secure Epic's future. Epic would not be Disney’s first potential acquisition target. In 2023, it was reported that Disney was interested in pursuing a purchase of Electronic Arts , but nothing ever came of that, and now EA has been sold to Saudi Arabia's PIF. Beyond Disney's investment in Epic for Fortnite, some of Disney's shows, like The Mandalorian, use Epic’s Unreal Engine to project scenes onto LED screens surrounding the physical set. D'Amaro is a big believer in video games and has said he wants to do more in gaming going forward . Wall Street is looking for some kind of catalyst for Disney's stock, and many have said further investments into tech and gaming could be a way to help get Disney's stock price out of its 10-year slump. Disney stock exploded during COVID, but is actually lower today than it was a decade ago. D'Amaro has floated numerous ideas for further Disney integration into Fortnite, including giving players the ability to book Disney cruises or watch a Disney movie on the platform . Fortnite is a big push from Disney in gaming, but it's just one small piece. Disney today has nine gaming franchises that have individually earned more than $1 billion .

title: The Street Fighter Movie’s Most Obscure Easter Egg Is For True Fighting Game Nerds
text: Ahead of its release later this month, marketing for the Street Fighter movie has focused on deep references to the long-running fighting game series. How deep? We already knew that fighting game legend Justin Wong--alongside Michael "IFC Yipes" Mendoza--was making a cameo as one of the inmates who watches Ryu take on Blanka in a prison fight , but even his prisoner costume hides one heck of an Easter egg. Any fighting game fan will instantly recognize it: on Wong's neck, you can spot the number 37, a reference to the legendary Evo Moment 37 . In a new behind-the-scenes video, Wong detailed the time he spent on the Street Fighter movie set getting fake dirt and dressing up for his cameo. If you're unfamiliar with the significance of the fake 37 tattoo his character sports, it's a deep-cut nod to what many consider one of the greatest fighting game comebacks in history. Back in 2004, Wong faced off against Daigo Umehara, and with his chosen brawler, Chun-Li, down to just a sliver of health and backed into a corner, Wong parried over a dozen attacks from Umehara's Ken Masters and found the perfect window to counter the onslaught. https://youtu.be/ssipFrggf58 It's a moment that has yet to be equaled within the fighting game community, with the clip earning an obscene number of views over the decades. This is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the accuracy the Street Fighter movie is aiming for, as the film embraces the unique look of the Capcom games with its choice of costumes, special attacks, and goofy hairstyles that double as the perfect popcorn bucket . Chun-Li actress Callina Liang even went the extra mile to get into fighting shape for the movie, focusing on conditioning her thighs to look impressively muscular and memorizing Chun-Li's various attacks. On the audio side, composers Leo Birenberg and Zach Robinson (Cobra Kai) have even used classic video game soundtracks for the film's score, including a new version of Guile's theme that fits everything . Street Fighter hits theaters on October 16. Street Fighter Movie: Release Date, Cast, And Everything We Know So Far View Images

title: Activision Could Be Giving Halo Something It Hasn’t Had In Years: A Clean Slate
text: Halo has a new home at Activision following recent changes at Xbox , and while it's still early days, Activision has reportedly proposed a total reboot for the series. This would be a fresh start, moving away from the convoluted Halo lore built up over the last 25 years through various games and spin-off media. That's according to sources who spoke to Rebs Gaming, who also stressed that nothing is concrete right now. Call of Duty developer Sledgehammer Games presented conceptual prototypes for a free-to-play multiplayer game and a story campaign built in the Infinity Ward engine, and it's believed the studio will lead development. "Activision is building a development team for the next Halo game, and based on my information, that team could be built within Sledgehammer Games. I'm also told they created the prototypes in the Infinity Ward engine. This doesn't confirm the game will be developed in Call of Duty's engine instead of Unreal Engine, but the prototypes indicate it's definitely possible. Apparently, Activision's idea for the campaign project was a soft reboot that doesn't follow Halo Infinite's story, but also doesn't retcon established canon," Rebs Gaming said. "However, it sounds like plans are changing. I'm told they discarded their original project ideas for a full Halo game." https://youtu.be/wPWqTRrCgX0 Rebs Gaming added that this means a sequel to Halo Infinite is unlikely and that "at least some of Halo's story" will be rebooted. One major criticism of Halo after its original developer, Bungie, left the franchise and handed it over to 343 Industries/Halo Studios was that the franchise shifted away from telling standalone stories. Halo books and media were supplementary material that added to the franchise, but weren't essential to the overall narrative. But with Halo Studios, there was a period of mandatory homework for fans as novels, comics, and spin-off games featured crucial plot points and new characters. For example, the Forerunner history in Halo 4 and the appearance of Blue Team in Halo 5 required outside reading to understand what was going on, while later games jettisoned major villains like the Didact and Jul 'Mdama, resulting in a messy lore with abrupt resets. In related Halo news, former franchise director Frank O’Connor offered plenty of advice to Activision as it builds the new game, including pitfalls it should avoid.

title: PS5’s Exciting New Zelda-Like Kena Game Just Got Delayed
text: Developer Ember Lab has announced that its upcoming PS5 game Kena: Scars of Kosmora, the sequel to 2021's much-loved Kena: Bridge of Spirits, has been delayed. The game-- which gives off major Zelda vibes --was previously set to release this year , but now it's been delayed to 2027. In a blog post , the developers said they need more time to "deliver a top-notch game that exceeds the quality" of Bridge of Spirits. "Pushing our release into 2027 gives us the ability to really polish the expanded game experience we want to deliver," the studio said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhgxkBxiCyg Scars of Kosmora is a linear adventure game, just like the 2021 entry, but the sequel has a "broader and deeper scope," the studio said. "We hope you’re just as excited to jump into Kena’s next adventure as we are to share it with you. We’ve been working hard to fill it with the wonder, charm, and challenge fans have come to expect," the team added. "We appreciate your patience and support as we take the time for Scars of Kosmora to be the evolution of Kena’s journey and experience we want to deliver." In Scars of Kosmora, main character Kena is now a seasoned spirit guide and embarks on a journey to the island of Kosmora to find a "cure for her affliction and to reconnect with a friend from her past." The island holds a "powerful corruption" that fractures her staff, so Kena adopts a new method of manipulating the elements to her advantage. "On her journey, Kena discovers and nurtures memorable spirit companions-- whose powers she will harness to solve puzzles and defeat enemies using new elemental abilities," reads a line from the game's description. 2021's Bridge of Spirits was released initially on PS4, PS5, and PC, and later came to Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S in 2024. A Switch 2 edition arrived in March this year. Kosmora has been confirmed only for PS5 and PC so far.

title: GTA 6’s Weather System Sounds Like A Big Step Up
text: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 includes a number of updates and improvements over the developer's past games, and that includes new weather systems. Rockstar's vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar, Owen Shepherd, told Game Informer that the studio has "re-engineered" the studio's weather system to "make everything more more localized and persistent." He said the goal was to make the weather in GTA 6's setting of Leonida--a stand-in for Florida--feel "dynamically solid and achieve a sense of scale" that the studio has never done before. GTA 6 launches on November 19. What that means in practice is that GTA 6 will have "fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map" to provide a "broad spectrum of weather" in the game. Florida is known for its heat and humidity, along with its localized and fast-moving rain systems. Look one direction and you may see bright sunshine. Look the other and you could see a downpour. GTA 6 will replicate this with localized rain showers, along with rainbows that appear. Additionally, places where it recently rained in the game will remain wet, with puddles also popping up. GTA 6 also has a new wind system that includes "offshore breezes after sunset, convectional updrafts, and occlusion from buildings,” Shepherd said. “Hair and debris will swirl around on rooftops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps.” GTA 6 will also include tropical storms and hurricanes, along with thunder and lightning. Shepherd did not, however, get into how GTA 6's new weather systems could affect gameplay. Florida is known to experience devastating hurricanes, but it remains to be seen if, for example, a hurricane could knock down structures or trees. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, priced at $80 for its standard edition and $100 for the Ultimate Edition. Rockstar is also selling a $400 collector's edition that includes a bunch of physical goodies, but not the game.

title: Blizzard Isn’t Fixing Diablo 4 Season 15’s Biggest Bug
text: Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced. Hellfire Torch is a new Unique charm that counts as an extra set charm and comes with some great beneficial stats, like +All Skills, +All Stats, and +All Resistances. Players can usually only have one Unique charm equipped at a time, but Hellfire Torch breaks that rule, allowing players to use it and another Unique charm. That's strong on its own, but there is currently a bugged interaction with Hellfire Torch that is allowing players to equip two Unique charms in addition to Hellfire Torch instead of one, granting even higher levels of power. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2L55dgNzpQ8 The bug seems to stem from Hellfire Torch being used first alongside the Seal of the Golden Epiphany, which allows players to equip up to three Unique charms. However, players are later swapping out Golden Epiphany for the Mythic Seal of the Diamond Mind, a seal that reduces the number of charms needed for set bonuses, but are still able to benefit from having additional Unique charms equipped. That, in turn, allows players to gain advantages from a full five-piece set bonus, Hellfire Torch, and two Unique charms all at once. Now, Diablo 4 design director Dan Tanguay in a forum post said Blizzard is aware of the bug and said Hellfire Torch' s current behavior is "beyond what was originally intended." That being said, Blizzard will be letting it ride this season as it works towards a fix in the future. "We know many players have spent significant time earning the Hellfire Torch and building characters around it," Tanguay said. "Because of that, we want to be thoughtful about making adjustments mid-season that could disrupt those investments." Tanguay continued: "We've also seen the positive reception to the Hellfire Torch itself from many players. The item has created a lot of excitement this season, and we've taken note of the feedback from those who have enjoyed earning it and incorporating it into their builds. While we don't have anything to announce today, it is something we're considering for the future, which makes it even more important that we fully understand and address this interaction the right way." The post states Blizzard will continue to investigate the issue so that any future changes will be "implemented correctly and behave as intended." Players in Season 15 just might be stronger than ever before. Alongside the bugged Hellfire Torch interaction, players can also use this trick to get around the game's crafted Mythic item restriction and fully deck themselves out in Mythic gear. It's just the last development in what has been one of Diablo 4's wildest, and most surprising, seasons yet. Season 15, Hell's Legacy, introduced all kinds of new content based on previous Diablo games, including boss fights against Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto ripped straight from earlier entries in the franchise. It's also filled to the brim with secrets upon secrets , including a showdown with the cow god Moophisto and even the return of the secret pony level, Whimsyshire, from Diablo 3. Diablo 4 will continue to receive new seasons going forward, but won't be getting new expansions , as Blizzard instead shifts its focus to Diablo 5 . A new Diablo 4 class , the Amazon, will release as standalone DLC in the first half of 2027.

title: PS5 Just Got A PS5 Pro-Like AI Upgrade, But Don’t Expect It Everywhere Yet
text: The base PS5 console is no slouch when it comes to games, but compared to the PS5 Pro, it doesn't pack the same visual punch. That could change soon, as Sony has unveiled a new AI-upscaling upgrade for the older machine called Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). Like PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), it is designed to make games look sharper and maximize performance. While PSSR will still remain the "gold standard" for what Sony games can look like on PS5 Pro, QSSR looks like it'll offer a noticeable improvement on PS5. A result of the AI graphics collaboration with AMD, Sony says that it offers a "streamlined neural network architecture" for games. The only catch? For now, only two PS5 games will support it: Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei --which is getting a new Complete Edition this month. Here are a few samples of it in action: https://youtu.be/RcFYsDKbAIk https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E929-XwrS_Q "QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan's epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel's Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5," head of technology at Insomniac Games, Mike Fitzgerald, wrote in a PS Blog post . Jasmin Patry, lead rendering engineer at Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch Productions, added that QSSR excels at "resolving the fine details" in characters and environments that previously wasn't possible on the base PS5. Both PS5 exclusives are receiving a patch today to add QSSR as an additional graphics option, and Sony says it will be offered to all PlayStation developers soon. If it's implemented widely and across many more games, QSSR could become a big selling point for the PS5, as the console will be six years old in November. Price hikes have made it more expensive to jump into the current console generation, and for anyone who can afford the $900 PS5 Pro , stock seems increasingly harder to find as demand begins to outpace supply. In Japan, potential consumers are now being asked to enter a lottery system and prove they've played at least 60 hours over the last two years on their current PS5 console. In comparison, an improved gaming experience on a regular PS5 console sounds like it makes financial sense--even if the console was much cheaper when it first launched in 2020.

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Clever Solution To One Of PC Gaming’s Biggest Annoyances
text: Early access for Gears of War: E-Day has kicked off for anyone who bought the Premium Edition, and if you're on PC, you're probably dreading the traditional shader compilation wait that comes with it. There's good news, as Gears of War: E-Day supports a neat feature on this platform that cuts down on that process significantly. Called Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD), it addresses how modern games rely on shaders to calculate how light, shadows, reflections, and textures should look on screen. This usually involves you sitting for a while when you first boot up a game after installing it, resulting in the infamous "Compiling Shaders" loading bar. In comparison, ASD is like buying a Gundam model kit that's already assembled, right out of the box. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xTxwN-Ck1Zw ASD pre-translates and delivers shader files directly to your device ahead of time, so you wait mere seconds. It also works across a wide variety of systems, and while I haven't installed Gears of War: E-Day on my main PC yet, I did load it up on my Asus Xbox ROG Ally X. The shader compilation waiting time was around 20 seconds, far better than waiting up to 15 minutes as I've experienced with other new games. It's also worth noting that ASD works with multiple hardware configurations, including devices powered by AMD, Intel, Nvidia, and Qualcomm. Gears of War: E-Day will be the first game to support ASD across Windows devices, and it's currently available for users with AMD graphics cards. Owners of Nvidia GPUs will receive ASD-compatible drivers shortly after E-Day launches. I was slaying the Locust, not my patience. While our impression of the multiplayer portion of Gears of War: E-Day is still coming, the campaign is a mostly solid excuse to take cover and pop some Locust heads. "For better or worse, E-Day is distinctly Gears, and I had a good time with it, even if the story is disappointing and the open areas are fairly dull," Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot's Gears of War: E-Day review . "But that’s all it is: a good game, propped up by combat that hasn’t changed all that much over the past 20 years. That’s enough to skate by, but I wish Gears of War would dig deeper."

title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Compromise Scale For Detail, Rockstar Says
text: Rockstar's games are known for their impressive attention to detail, along with their massive scopes, and GTA 6 is seemingly going to up the ante in that regard. Rockstar boss Aaron Garbut said in an interview that a developer might compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction "but not with this project." "We went the other way," he told Game Informer . "Everything is dialed up--detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction, and density." He went on to say Rockstar has never "created anything close to this before." "As the pressure for us on this project is huge, we dealt with that by doing our best to overdeliver," Garbut said. Lucia and Jason in GTA 6. No game can have everything, though, and GTA 6 is no different. The game takes place in Florida stand-in Leonida but doesn't feature Walt Disney World , for example, but Rockstar says the game will deliver the "full Florida experience." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game has reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies, generating more than $570 million in pre-sales. Also this week, Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 will have more than 170 animal species , including cane toads and monkeys. We also learned that GTA 6 has a new dynamic weather system .

title: Former Steelers Head Coach Reveals Minecraft City He’s Been Building For 12 Years
text: Mike Tomlin served as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2007-2025, which is a remarkably long tenure in the NFL. During more than half of that time, Tomlin was secretly working on a massive Minecraft city, and he's now revealing it to the general public. In the first episode of his deep dive into the Minecraft city--and the first video on his YouTube channel--Tomlin shared how the city began, initially with his kids' participation, but as they grew older, it became more and more of a focus for him alone. Much like the Steelers' roster changed every season, Tomlin remained the constant. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_h_pQ1-5iQg As you can see in the video, Mike Tomlin put an enormous amount of effort and time into building this city, not only creating the skyscrapers and nearby neighborhoods, but also sports stadiums. He said in the first episode that he'd go into more detail on these stadiums later, but the city includes a baseball field and a soccer pitch, alongside the obvious football field. His son Mayce also shared that Tomlin would sometimes take his PlayStation, presumably due to a sudden creative spark. https://twitter.com/maycetomlin/status/2105457694148821231 Tomlin has a lot more time to focus on Minecraft since resigning as the Steelers' head coach following the 2025 season. During his tenure, the team famously never had a losing season, which might just change this year with a grandfather at quarterback and a defense that has major issues stopping the run. Pittsburgh native Mike McCarthy is the team's new head coach, and it's unclear if he plays Minecraft.

title: PUBG: Black Budget Canceled, Joining Live-Service Graveyard
text: PUBG publisher Krafton has pulled the plug on its extraction shooter spin-off PUBG: Black Budget . Announced less than a year ago and already through several closed alpha tests, the publisher's reasoning for the cancellation is simple: it believes Black Budget simply wasn't fun enough to keep potential players engaged. "After reviewing the project's development status and future direction, we concluded that its current direction would not allow us to deliver an experience players could enjoy over the long term," Krafton wrote in a Steam update . "We have therefore made the difficult decision to end development of PUBG: Black Budget. PUBG Studios will carry what we learned from development and testing into future projects, continuing to listen to players as we explore new gameplay experiences." Black Budget is the second PUBG spin-off to get the axe, following the demise of the tactical shooter PUBG: Blindspot in March. While the game launched in early access, Krafton closed it down after two months, saying it was "no longer able to sustainably provide the level of experience" it set out to deliver. PUBG: Black Budget Krafton's reasons for cancelling Black Budget aren't without merit. If it had been fully released, Black Budget would likely have faced an uphill battle, as the extraction shooter genre is perceived as a niche market dominated by a handful of games, while the live-service video game graveyard is full of recent projects that failed to find an audience. Many games launch with strong momentum, but they struggle to retain those initial player numbers, and their audiences shrink quickly. Just look at Highguard , as the free-to-play shooter lasted just over a month before it shut down. PUBG franchise director Taeseok Jang recently reflected on the struggles of Highguard and other live-service games, commenting on how hard it is to succeed in that space. Krafton has another PUBG spin-off in the works, the grindhouse-themed multiplayer shooter Ded.Net. Announced back in August during Gamescom, it's currently being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin-based studio PUBG Madison.

title: Uncharted 5 Is Reportedly In Development And Will Feature Nathan Drake
text: Naughty Dog is focused on releasing its first new IP since 2013's The Last of Us in Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , but a new report suggests it is also busy with the revival of its biggest franchise. According to MP1st , and corroborated by VGC , Naughty Dog could be developing Uncharted 5, a sequel to a series that last saw an entry in 2017. The report claims that Uncharted: The Lost Legacy director Shaun Escayag is leading the project, after briefly leaving Naughty Dog to work on Crystal Dynamic's ill-fated Avengers . It's suggested that Uncharted 5 will be the studio's next release after Intergalactic, with The Last of Us 3 coming afterwards. That would align with Naughty Dog's recent announcement that it is working on multiple new Last of Us projects. The report doesn't have too many details on the game itself, outside of mentioning that the series' main protagonist, Nathan Drake, will be present in some capacity. That could leave the door open for Cassie Drake, Nathan's daughter who appears at the end of Uncharted: 4 A Thief's End, to potentially take over as the series' lead going forward. This latest entry is also apparently not a remake of any sort, with Naughty Dog reportedly shelving those plans a long time ago. Uncharted 4 was positioned as the definitive end for Nathan Drake's story when it released in 2016, but Naughty Dog has repeatedly suggested that it is not done with the franchise . Escayag himself stated in 2022 that it's a world the studio wants to see more of, saying “I think we can say for certain that we can never say never." In February of this year, he posted a vague Instagram photo of a cannon in a tropical environment that was captioned “research," suggesting that he might be working on something related to Uncharted. When Uncharted 5 might release is anyone's guess, but it's more likely that it'll arrive on the PlayStation 6 given that Sony is expected to release its next-generation console sometime in 2028. Intergalatic, the studio's most imminent project, will be revealed in full in 2027, with a release window still unknown.

title: Xbox Is Paying A Lot Less Than Normal For Kojima’s Physint, Possibly Under $200 Million – Report
text: New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has made a lot of big moves since taking over for Phil Spencer in the role, one of which was signing Hideo Kojima's new spy-thriller game, Physint , after Sony walked away from it. According to The New York Times , Xbox's agreement with Kojima was "substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game." What exactly would be typical, however, is unknown, because game studios are incredibly secretive about budgets. The money figures for Physint have been a point of contention, with unconfirmed reports that Physint's budget at Sony was $400 million. This has never been confirmed, but it was also reported that one of the reasons Sony opted to drop Kojima and Physint was that the game was over budget and late . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NzzdyORdg80 Windows Central's Jez Corden said he was told by first-hand sources with "direct knowledge of the contracts" for Physint at Xbox that the real number is "far lower." He said the deal between Xbox and Kojima amounts to only a "fraction" of the reported figure. The Game Business reporter Chris Dring, who originated the $400 million rumor, said he was only speculating, and the internet did what the internet does. He subsequently stated that he understands that Xbox is paying "far, far less," and "possibly even below $200 million." Xbox's deal with Kojima for Physint also covers film and TV adaptations . Physint stars Bill Skarsgard as its lead , along with Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe. The game doesn't have a release date or any footage as of yet. Kojima believes Physint could become his most commercial game yet . Kojima said he got the idea for Physint in part due to the overwhelming fan demand for another Metal Gear game . He no longer works at Konami and couldn’t make a new Metal Gear, but the interest from fans inspired him to make a “new action espionage game” that became Physint. Sony originally announced that it would publish Physint, but the company told Kojima over Zoom that it was terminating the deal . Kojima's previous game franchise with Sony, Death Stranding, reportedly barely broke even . Sharma also briefly discussed Xbox's relationship with PlayStation, saying the two companies currently work together and that will continue under her leadership. "Competition and collaboration can coexist," she said. Physint is not the only Kojima game that Xbox is publishing, as the company is also partnered with the studio for the horror game OD .

title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Already Being Patched For Being Too Bright
text: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launched for free earlier this week, and has since been subject to debate over whether its visual changes have been for the better. One aspect that has routinely dominated the conversation is how overly bright the remaster makes the game look, and it's evident developer CD Projekt Red agrees that it went too far. A patch for Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, and the Xbox Play Anywhere version of the game on PC has been released that makes "various lighting adjustments" across the game, among other things. CD Projekt Red detailed the patch on social media , stating that the team is working on another hotfix for PC that will address a save game issue that numerous players have reported. The brief patch notes can be found below. https://youtu.be/_oEdB5S2d3U?si=v_wBtlRpVoS4Waq- Fixed an issue where DLSS was unavailable in the Xbox Play Anywhere version of the game on PC Made various lighting adjustments, including fixing some interiors that appeared too dark Made various other adjustments to ensure parity with the PC version The patch isn't being released for other PC versions because it's likely that the fix centers around the game's bloom setting. It's one that PC players have suggested turning off to regain some contrast in the game's image, but one that wasn't available for players on consoles. A different hotfix released on October 1 has a slightly different list of notes: Fixed an issue where the game couldn't be saved or loaded if the path to the Documents folder contained special characters. Fixed an issue where voiceover audio could become significantly quieter than other in-game audio after navigating through the pause menu tabs. Made various visual adjustments in Velen, including tweaks to Bloom, vegetation lighting, saturation, and Path Tracing lighting. Reverted a change that caused significant performance and visual issues with HairWorks enabled for some users. Fixed an issue where marketing telemetry settings weren't saved properly. Fixed an issue where it wasn't possible to launch the Classic (1.32) version of the game. This patch doesn't introduce a toggle, but likely toggles it off for all console players. If you're playing on Nintendo Switch 2, however, you won't be able to benefit from the fix just yet. The bloom setting doesn't fix everything though. Players have still taken issue with the game's HDR implementation, path tracing visual presentation, and overall system performance on PC. CD Projekt Red hasn't yet commented on whether it is planning to make changes to those areas, but this patch does indicate that they are aware of the most glaring issues players are facing. The Witcher 3 Remastered released as a free update for all versions of the game, introducing enhanced character animations, world detail, improved combat and role-playing systems, and more. An expansion for the 11 year old game, Songs of the Past , is scheduled to release in 2027 and will tie into the events of the The Witcher 4 , which is currently in development.

title: Resident Evil Director’s Next Movie Is Called The Flood But It’s Not About Halo, Adds Jennifer Lawrence
text: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie is a critical and commercial hit, but the director is not jumping right into a sequel, and may never. Instead, his next project is called The Flood, and while The Flood are well-known to gamers in Halo's lore , Cregger's new movie has nothing to do with Halo--though it does involve aliens. Cregger is known for keeping secrets about his movies, and he’s not saying much about what to expect from The Flood beyond that it’s a sci-fi movie set in deep space. Dread Central reported that The Flood is "very Alien-esque," with the story focusing on a deep-space ship captain who, with her crew, investigates a strange signal "from a distant world." The signal leads the crew to an "alien artifact that warps time, reality, and their sanity, forcing them into a confrontation with an incomprehensible intelligence." Oscar-winning actor Jennifer Lawrence has signed on for The Flood, according to Variety . Though her exact role in the film remains unknown, she will likely play the lead, the ship captain. This is somewhat familiar ground for Lawrence, as she starred in 2016's sci-fi movie Passengers, in which she played a character aboard a spaceship opposite Chris Pratt. Cregger is re-teaming with Warner Bros./New Line for The Flood; he previously made the successful thriller Weapons at the studio. He said in a statement that Lawrence is a "one-of-a-kind" talent and that he's excited to work with her. In addition to Warner Bros./New Line, Cregger is working with Steven Spielberg's Amblin Entertainment and Roy Lee's Vertigo on The Flood. As for Lawrence, she earned her first Academy Award nomination for 2010's Winter's Bone. She won an Oscar for 2012's Silver Linings Playbook, and also picked up nominations for American Hustle and Joy. She is also known for playing Katniss in the Hunger Games movie series. As for a possible sequel to Resident Evil, given the movie has made so much money and strong reviews, many are expecting another entry. That may happen, but Cregger has said he is done with franchise movies , even though he does have ideas for a sequel . “I’m doing this [Resident Evil], and that’s it for me. I’m not going to go tackle any other franchises," he said.

title: 007 First Light’s Free Expansion Gives Bond A Driving License To Kill
text: 007 First Light developer IO Interactive has revealed a major new free update for the James Bond game, which is now available across PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. Extended Operations adds new missions, the Valhalla Protocol, a photo mode, New Game+, new weapons, outfits, and more. Here's a closer look at everything that's new: Valhalla Protocol https://youtu.be/yRF4IXmNixo The main event of Extended Operations, Valhalla Protocol brings back Bond's signature Aston Martin Valhalla ride for a race against the clock in Slovakia. The track will have four different versions that you can test your driving skills in, and when putting the pedal to the metal isn't enough, you can always rely on its arsenal of guns and missile launchers to help you earn a first-place finish--far better than a boring Formula One race. Photo mode Is that a Great Gatsby meme pose? 007 First Light has no shortage of exciting moments, and you can capture them in all their digital glory in the game's new photo mode. Similar to the photo modes found in many modern games, you can set up Bond and use unique filters, custom light setups, exclusive poses, and much more to take the perfect shot. New operation: Jungle Heist Welcome to the Jungle Heist, we've got guns and flames. A new mission for 007 First Light, Jungle Heist tasks Bond with infiltrating a jungle villa, finding out who's concealing the codes to a secret safe, retrieving its contents, and then fighting your way up to the extraction point. New weapons Locked and loaded. Bond's arsenal is also being updated with two new weapons: the Squire Marksman rifle and the Storm 12 shotgun. New outfits For your fashion eyes only. Time to dress for success--or big-budget Hollywood explosions--with a fresh set of Q Division threads. Bond can don some casual clothes with the Leisure Beam outfit, posh it up with the First Class tuxedo, and blend in with the Observant Spy ensemble. New Game Plus Time for a Bond replay. You can replay the entire 007 First Light campaign--which is really good!-- and you can also choose to wear different outfits that you've unlocked from your first session with the game. 00 difficulty mode Prepare to die, a lot. Think you've earned your 00 number? You can put your skills to the test with the 00 difficulty mode, which is designed to punish even the smallest mistake. Resources are more limited, enemies are deadly, and the mode is billed as the ultimate challenge for players. IO Interactive has steadily added new content to 007 First Light since it launched in May, and Amazon Game Studios boss Jeff Gattis recently suggested that a sequel is a matter of when , not if. The game reached an impressive milestone of 4 million units sold in August 2026 across PC and consoles--minus Switch 2, as 007 First Light is still MIA on that platform. The Switch 2 edition has been delayed several times, and it's now expected to arrive in March 2027 as IO works on getting it ready for the Nintendo handheld. "As Hollywood seems uncertain about where to take Bond next, IO Interactive’s debut effort is supremely confident," Mark Delaney wrote in GameSpot's 007 First Light review .

title: How Long Is Gears of War: E-Day – Mission List And Hours Played
text: Gears of War: E-Day is almost here--unless you're hopping in a few days early with the Premium Edition--and if you're looking to try out the campaign, you can settle in for a few days of action and chainsaw executions. While Gears of War: E-Day is primarily a linear cover-based shooter, the game also sprinkles in some semi-open-world environments for you to explore between missions, giving you the opportunity to hunt down collectibles, upgrades, and take part in side missions. Here’s how long it’ll take you to beat Gears of War: E-Day. How long to beat Gears of War: E-Day depending on your play style If you tackle the Gears of War: E-Day campaign on normal difficulty, do a little bit of collectibles hunting and take part in the game's non-story missions, expect the campaign to take 10-14 hours to complete. In my own playthrough, I motored through the campaign and finished it in 11 hours, occasionally stopping along the way to track down a hidden item, find an upgrade pack for my arsenal, and take part in a side quest. I'd done roughly 60% of that content before I reached the end, and Gears of War: E-Day has a war journal that provides a very comprehensive list of things you missed in each mission, so you can go back and find them for a completionist run. That's a fairly standard playthrough time for a game in this series, and once you've rolled credits, the various multiplayer modes look like they'll consume plenty of your hours. You can increase the difficulty and spend more time in the campaign, but on higher challenge levels, enemies can be bullet-sponges that quickly burn through your stock of spare lives. Horde Siege looks like an especially enjoyable timesink, as this new take on the Gears of War horde mode revolves around three teams of four players taking on waves of enemies, co-operating with each other to accomplish objectives, and survive against increasingly overwhelming odds. Gears of War: E-Day mission list The campaign for Gears of War: E-Day is spread across five acts, each comprising several chapters. Acts 1 and 5 are the shortest of the bunch, while Acts 2-4 are lengthy, meaty parts of the overall narrative. You could easily do an Act per night, and spread them out over a week. title: Control Resonant Has Finally Gotten The One Thing It’s Missing (But Only On PC)
text: There's a lot to love about Control Resonant, from its delightfully weird world to its intriguing story, but visually, the game offers some jaw-dropping visuals and art direction. From the Hiss hovering in the air to the tastefully red atmosphere when you venture into dangerous zones, every frame of the game is begging for some virtual photography. The only problem? There's no photo mode yet, and developer Remedy Entertainment only plans to add it in a November update. And that's just too long to wait! Fortunately, if you're on PC, you can mod a photo mode for yourself. On Nexus Mods , user Kkyleeb21 has developed a robust toolset for nailing the perfect shot that, when active, switches the game engine to its built-in free camera and freezes time. Designed to be similar to Alan Wake 2's photo mode, the Control Resonant version offers everything you could ask for with its virtual camera. You can switch between presets, set exposure and depth of field, crop the image, and use one of six filters to make the scene look just right. Control Resonant players on Xbox Series X|S and PS5 will have to wait until November to start documenting their Altered World Event journey through New York, as Remedy said in a recent blog post that it wanted to prioritize game development first and then add a photo mode in a later update. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f1LEHPr8e_o&pp=0gcJCS4MAYcqIYzv "The Photo Mode for Control Resonant is something we’ve been cooking for a while," Remedy wrote . "We even consulted some talented virtual photographers from the community to help us make it the best it can be. The reason Photo Mode didn’t release on launch is because we needed to prioritize making sure the game was in the best possible shape. We've seen gorgeous virtual photographs you’ve already taken – but once the Photo Mode releases, you can really go to town. We expect to release Photo Mode sometime in November." A new update for the game has also gone live, adding an enhanced New Game+ mode and much more. Remedy says that, on top of recent gameplay balance tweaks, the new patch includes many bug fixes, adds extra polish, and throws in a few quality-of-life improvements. Control Resonant Game Update 1.4.0 New Game ++ You can now play an infinite number of runs of CONTROL Resonant in New Game ++ Added the Build Power number to the Loadout screen on the bottom left so that players can easily see their Power level instead of having to find it buried in the Stats & Effects menu It's worth saying here that if you are below the enemy level, you are going to have a tougher time with combat, so keep doing side quests, explore twisted Manhattan, and level up! The HUD will have a little notification icon to indicate that you have new things to buy or upgrade in The Gap Added a feature that when you pin materials you need to acquire for upgrades, you can see if these materials are available at the Vendor by looking at the Vendor icon on the Map (instead of having to go to the Vendor to see their wares) Unknown Zone - Decreased the overall amount of combat and intensity by 10%-15% Added a separate volume slider for radio dialogue. You can now customize the audio balance between speakers/headphones and the DualSense controller speaker Added a new option in the Assist Mode - Power Core Charge Duration: Added a 100-300% Power Core Charge duration multiplier Many fixes to map markers either sticking around too long or being in the wrong place and not clearing correctly. We are sure we still missed a few of these, though Fixed a VFX issue where framerate could drop during the Artist Resonant fight when she does her special attack Added “Mute copyrighted music” option to turn off Apocalyptica’s “Upperhand” intro credits song (It’s a great track, so why would you) Added a Tutorial about the Rush ability removing status effects Fixed over-saturated HDR highlights in AgX (tonemapper) Fixed a multitude of subtitle and VO issues across the game Several specific performance optimizations, mainly targeting PC minimum and recommended specs Polish on all aspects of the game, including audio, dialogue timing, subtitle timing, animation, lighting, code, mission polish, UI, and so on Added support for Razer haptics. The game will trigger many gameplay events like using melee, taking damage, etc., and trigger effects on Razer peripherals

title: Ubisoft’s Massive Entertainment Rebrand Has Made The Name Much More Literal And Slightly Confusing
text: After folding several of its studios into " Creative Houses " earlier this year, Ubisoft has announced a rebranding for Creative House 2, which might be slightly confusing. The branch that is home to almost all of Ubisoft's Tom Clancy-branded games, Creative House 2 will now be known as Massive Entertainment, which is also the name of one of Ubisoft's longest-serving studios. Massive Entertainment, as a studio, will still exist within Massive Entertainment the Creative House, and this arm of Ubisoft will continue to grow existing IP and work on new projects, like the upcoming March of Giants. "Starting today, development teams responsible for these franchises in Montréal, Paris, Sweden, and Toronto will operate under the Massive Entertainment brand, bringing together their creative and technology expertise to shape its future, grow these franchises and craft challenging experiences for dedicated player communities," Ubisoft said in a statement. Even the logo is massive. Massive Entertainment--the studio--was established in 1997 in Sweden, and it was acquired in 2002 by Vivendi. After Activision and Vivendi merged in 2008, the developer was sold to Ubisoft and has remained with the publisher ever since. The developer has been a hitmaker for Ubisoft, assisting Ubisoft Montreal on major titles such as Assassin's Creed Revelations and Far Cry 3, while also developing two entries in The Division series. Its most recent release was the divisive Star Wars Outlaws in 2024, and the studio is currently working on The Division 3 . This rebranding follows in the footsteps of Creative House 1, which is known as Vantage Studios. This Ubisoft subsidiary--in which Tencent owns a major stake --is responsible for Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six, and in total, there are five Creative Houses and one Creative Network that provides production support for the various studios. Earlier this year, Ubisoft teased that several new IP are in development, but the restructuring hasn't been smooth sailing for the people working at the publisher. Cost-cutting measures have resulted in the cancellation of games like the Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake , the shutdown of several Ubisoft studios , a return-to-office mandate, and numerous layoffs across the entire company.
